notes: Each appliance subcategory is its own category build with independent spec fields, anchors, and source pools.

tier_anchors.notes: Miele anchors above Bosch 800: best-in-category service rate (5.6%), 20-yr tested design life, vertical integration, 3 full spray arms. Bosch 800: best drying (zeolite/CrystalDry), excellent reliability (7.8%), universal service ecosystem. Both have strong expert consensus.

8.2% service rate, largest third rack with 360° wash jets, Whirlpool service network (broadest US parts availability), 4-level wash action. Repair techs rate alongside Bosch as 'safe buy' for long-term repairability.

Full stainless tub, AutoAir drying (not zeolite), 46 dBA, same BSH platform reliability. Below 500/800 on drying tech, noise, rack adjustability. Represents the quality floor professionals cite (~$700-800 price point).

Whirlpool: acceptable floor per repair techs, simplest designs, most widely stocked parts in US, average everything else. Samsung: service ecosystem trap — 20-22% failure rate cited, proprietary parts with limited authorized service, repair techs unanimously warn against. Samsung scores below Whirlpool despite similar or better specs on paper because serviceability is catastrophic.
No calibration products. Reserved for brands with no US service infrastructure, active safety recalls, or documented structural defects making repair economically unviable.

quality.notes: All dishwashers $1,000+ use stainless. Stainless reduces noise ~10 dB, enables condensation drying, resists stains/odors. Hybrid = stainless walls + plastic bottom (Bosch 100). Reliable proxy for overall build tier.

Brushless inverter: 85-90% efficiency, 10K+ hour lifespan, sealed/moisture-resistant, variable speed. Brushed: 60-65% efficiency, 500-800 cycle brush life. LG vertically manufactures motors (noted in report).

Manual mesh = finer filtration, quieter, requires user maintenance (Bosch, Miele standard). Self-cleaning mesh = quieter than grinder (some KitchenAid). Grinder = louder, zero maintenance, older American standard. Filter neglect is most common cause of repairs per repair techs.

Miele and Cove use 3 independent spray arms (dedicated top arm over upper rack). BSH uses 2 arms + passive overhead sprinkler. Real cleaning difference at full loads per Yale/professional comparisons.
KitchenAid 360° Max Jets = largest with rotating wash jets (unique). Miele 3D fold-down tray creates clearance below. Bosch 800 MyWay = flexible configurations. No third rack = entry-level.
Miele G7000 = only brand with middle rack adjustable while loaded. Bosch RackMatic = 6 configurations (3 positions × 2 heights). Fixed racks on entry-level.

performance.notes: Most widely published and compared spec. 37 dBA (Miele Extra Quiet) to 56+ dBA (entry-level). Stainless tub reduces noise ~10 dB vs plastic. Manufacturer-reported dBA is self-certified but consistent with independent measurements.

Zeolite (CrystalDry/StarDry) = best for plastics, volcanic mineral absorbs moisture + releases heat to 176°F. Fan-assist (Miele CleanDry, Cove) = good. Auto-open (Bosch 500) = lets steam escape. Condensation = requires stainless tub. Heated element = energy-intensive, entry-level. IMPORTANT: Thermador base models (Emerald, Sapphire) use condensation, NOT zeolite — only Star Sapphire gets zeolite.
EPA ENERGY STAR database provides model-level kWh/year. Bosch 800 ~199, Miele G7000 ~200-210, KitchenAid premium ~220, Frigidaire budget ~240. Pre-2013 models up to 800 kWh.
ENERGY STAR threshold 3.2 gal/cycle. Viking 2.58, Beko 2.59, Bosch 3.15. Source: EPA certified product database.

durability.notes: Yale Appliance: 33,190 real service calls. 2026 data: Miele 5.6%, Bosch Benchmark 7.7%, Bosch 7.8%, Thermador 8.1%, KitchenAid 8.2%, GE 8.9%, GE Profile 10.3%, LG 11.6%, F&P 16.6%, Café 16.6%. Whirlpool/Frigidaire/Samsung absent (Yale premium-focused). Use multi-year trend where available.
Miele publishes 20-year design life (5,600 cycle test). Cove claims 20-year. Most others 7-12 years. Only score when manufacturer publishes a specific number.
Cove: 5-year full parts+labor (best in class). Miele: 2-year standard, 5-year on top models. Gaggenau: 2-year. Most others: 1-year. Warranty exclusion consistency rule (Rule 18) applies.

GE: owned national service network. Bosch/KitchenAid/Whirlpool: parts universally stocked, every independent tech works on them. Miele/LG: limited independent service centers (Miele proprietary + expensive). Samsung: parts ecosystem trap — owners in many markets cannot get repairs. This is the spec that separates Samsung from Whirlpool despite similar build quality.

Whirlpool/KitchenAid: broadest parts supply chain in US. Bosch: universally stocked. Miele: proprietary, available but expensive (90-day part warranty). Samsung/Haier: proprietary with limited availability — economically unviable repair is the failure mode.

scoring_rules: Health certs report-only, no composite impact (NSF/ANSI 184, UL 749)

BSH Platform Rule: Bosch, Thermador, and Gaggenau share the same dishwasher platform (BSH Group, NC factory). Service rate spread across all three is 0.4% — noise, not differentiation. Each product line scored separately (Rule 19) but report MUST disclose shared platform. Gaggenau price premium is design/UX, not construction.
Thermador line split: Star Sapphire (zeolite/StarDry) and Emerald/Sapphire (condensation drying) are different products with different scores per Rule 19.

Yale service rate is directional, not definitive: single-region (Boston/Cape Cod/Southern NH), premium-segment skew, brands like Whirlpool/Frigidaire/Samsung absent due to low sales volume. Disclose limitation in every report. Use multi-year trend data where available to smooth single-year spikes (e.g., LG 2026 roller issue).

Service ecosystem is a scored durability spec, not just a report finding. Parts availability + authorized service density directly affect whether a product can be repaired — this is functional lifespan, not convenience.

Score the product as sold in the US market: US warranty, US service network, US parts availability. European field performance data is valid evidence for Quality/Durability axes but service ecosystem scored on US buyer experience.
Manufacturer design life only scored when a specific number is published (Miele 20-yr/5,600 cycles, Cove 20-yr claim). Do not infer design life from warranty length.
Score base configuration per Rule 17. Bosch 500 and 800 are different products — do not average across a brand's lineup.
Corporate structure = report finding (BSH Group, Whirlpool/KitchenAid shared platform, GE/GE Profile/Café shared platform).

LG service rate volatility rule: when a single-year spike is attributed to one component (Yale: 2026 roller issue), report both the spike year and the multi-year trend. Do not anchor tier placement to a known anomaly year.

sources: Yale Appliance (Steve Sheinkopf) — 33,190 real service calls, brand-level service rates, multi-year trend data, published annually. Geographic limitation: Boston/Cape Cod/Southern NH, premium-segment skew.
Consumer Reports (80K+ subscriber reliability survey, controlled lab testing, paywalled but citable methodology)
Reviewed.com (UL-owned, Cambridge MA lab, AHAM/IEC protocols, numeric soil removal % scores — best public source for cleaning performance data)
CNET (Louisville KY lab, AHAM/IEC protocols, controlled environment testing)
Good Housekeeping Institute (AHAM standards committee participation, Seal of Approval is earned certification)
J.D. Power US Appliance Reliability Study (survey-based, not repair records — triangulation source)
r/appliancerepair (repair technician community, consistent consensus on brand reliability hierarchy)
Prudent Reviews (Yale data synthesis and independent analysis)
RepairClinic / ApplianceVideo / PartsDr (repair-focused YouTube, component-level diagnostics)
TWB YouTube (one Fisher & Paykel teardown — closest to component analysis in the category)
Individual owner reviews and forum posts
